section_summary: The section begins with the end of a wartime news digest on economic production, education, health, and communications in Japanese-controlled Southeast Asia. A Board of Economic Warfare letter then forwards the first volume of a June 1943 collection on Japanese occupation techniques. Its introduction surveys administrative and economic control, followed by the Meiji Constitution and ordinances establishing Japanese planning and occupation agencies.

subfiles.title: Wartime economic and administrative news digest, concluding pages
subfiles.about: Reports describe production, self-sufficiency, schooling, health, postal deposits, and communications across Japanese-controlled Southeast Asia.
subfiles.summary: The surviving digest entries cover rice and cotton cultivation, rubber products, iron and light industry, farming, schools, public health, and telegraph services. They also report Thai policy and wartime remittances. The first and last pages contain fragments of entries continued across the section boundaries.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting RR-7, Japanese Techniques of Occupation
subfiles.from: Rifat Tirana, Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: The Board of Economic Warfare sends the first volume of its occupation-techniques collection.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the Japan Proper volume and announces forthcoming volumes on Manchukuo, occupied China, and Thailand.

subfiles.title: Japanese Techniques of Occupation: Key Laws and Official Documents, title page
subfiles.from: Board of Economic Warfare, Reoccupation Division and Enemy Branch
subfiles.about: The title page identifies the restricted report and its issuing offices.
subfiles.summary: Identifies restricted report RR-7, copy 50, dated June 1943.

subfiles.title: Preface to Japanese Techniques of Occupation
subfiles.about: The preface explains the selection of laws and territories covered by the collection.
subfiles.summary: Explains that selected laws illustrate Japanese occupation methods and links occupied-area controls to those in Japan.

subfiles.title: Introduction to Japanese Techniques of Occupation
subfiles.about: The introduction analyzes Japanese political administration and control of finance, industry, trade, and agriculture in occupied territories.
subfiles.summary: The report describes Cabinet and military direction of nominally local governments, with Japanese control over external affairs and major resources. Its finance section traces military notes, central banks, exchange controls, and development companies. Further sections describe industrial cartels and strategic investment, controlled and barter trade, and agricultural purchasing, requisitioning, and crop shifts.

subfiles.title: Volume I: Japan Proper, title and table of contents
subfiles.about: The contents list the Japanese constitutional, administrative, military, economic, security, and financial documents reproduced in Volume I.
subfiles.summary: Volume title and contents enumerate the laws, ordinances, policy statements, and introductory notes arranged under eight subjects.

subfiles.title: Government: introductory note
subfiles.about: The note outlines the Meiji constitutional system and the military's growing dominance of Japan's government.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes imperial authority, the Diet's limits, military control, the Cabinet Planning Board, and the Greater East Asia Ministry.

subfiles.title: The Constitution of the Empire of Japan
subfiles.to: Japanese subjects and the Imperial Diet
subfiles.about: The reproduced Meiji Constitution sets out imperial powers, subjects' rights, the Diet, ministers, courts, finance, and amendment rules.
subfiles.summary: The text opens with the imperial promulgation and names the ministers who countersigned it. Seven chapters define the Emperor's executive, legislative, and military powers; qualified civil liberties and duties of subjects; the two houses of the Diet; ministers and Privy Council; courts; taxation and budgets; and constitutional amendment.

subfiles.title: The Cabinet Planning Board (Kikaku-in)
subfiles.about: Imperial Ordinance No. 605 establishes the Planning Board's mobilization and coordination responsibilities.
subfiles.summary: Defines the Board's planning, budget-review, and interagency coordination duties, then lists its staff, departments, and officers' responsibilities.

subfiles.title: Outline of the Organization of the Greater East Asia Ministry
subfiles.about: The announcement assigns responsibilities among the new ministry, Foreign Ministry, Home Ministry, and colonial governments.
subfiles.summary: Outlines the new ministry's bureaus and authority over occupied territories, while reallocating oversight of Korea, Taiwan, and Sakhalin.

subfiles.title: Organic Law of the Manchurian Affairs Bureau
subfiles.about: Imperial Ordinance No. 347 defines the Bureau's authority over Japanese administration and enterprises in Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: Assigns coordination, colonization, and oversight of the Kwantung Bureau and major railway and telecommunications companies; specifies personnel and duties.

subfiles.title: Ordinance Establishing the Kwantung Bureau
subfiles.about: Imperial Ordinance No. 348 establishes the Kwantung Bureau and prescribes its administrative, police, and personnel powers.
subfiles.summary: The ordinance places the bureau in Japan's embassy in Manchukuo and gives the ambassador authority over Kwantung Province and the South Manchuria Railway Zone. It establishes provincial and district offices, police and fire services, staffing, penalties, and emergency powers. Supplementary rules transfer existing Kwantung government personnel and references to the new bureau.

subfiles.title: Organic Law of the Asia Development Board
subfiles.about: The ordinance establishes a Cabinet agency to coordinate Japanese political, economic, and cultural activity in China.
subfiles.summary: Creates the Asia Development Board under the prime minister for the duration of the China conflict. It defines jurisdiction over policy, companies, and interagency coordination, then sets out departments, a liaison committee, staffing, officers' duties, and liaison offices.
